title: You stared at the assignment longer than you want to admit.
paragraphs: You stared at the assignment longer than you want to admit.
Not because you didn’t understand the instructions.
But because something in you knew… human logic wasn’t going to be enough this time.

You tried the usual approach. Research. Outlines. Rewriting sentences until they sounded “smart.” You even compared your work to others, hoping to find a pattern you could imitate. But the more you leaned on your own understanding, the heavier it felt.
And deep down, there was a quiet tension you couldn’t shake.
Because this wasn’t just about finishing a task.
It was about truth.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
There are assignments in life that are designed to expose the limits of human wisdom.
Moments where intellect reaches a ceiling—and God is the only way forward.
You felt it, didn’t you?
That subtle frustration.
That internal pressure.
That awareness that no matter how hard you think, something is missing.
God saw it.
You knew.
“Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to Him, and He will make your paths straight.” — Proverbs 3:5–6
Read that again.
Lean not on your own understanding.
That’s not a suggestion. That’s a command.

Because your mind, as sharp as it may be, is still shaped by limitation, bias, and sin. You can analyze, but you cannot see the full picture. You can construct arguments, but you cannot produce truth apart from the One who is Truth.
And this is where everything shifts.
Because the assignment in front of you is not just academic.
It’s spiritual.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
You were trained to rely on logic.
God is calling you to rely on Him.
And that feels uncomfortable… almost threatening to your sense of control.
Because divine wisdom requires surrender.
“If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to you.” — James 1:5
Not Google.
Not your past experience.
God.
But here’s the tension…
You don’t just lack wisdom in your assignment.
You lack wisdom in your life.
You’ve made decisions based on what “made sense” at the time.
You justified things.
Compromised in small ways.
Ignored convictions.
And told yourself it was reasonable.
But it wasn’t righteousness.
“Where is the wise person? Where is the teacher of the law? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?” — 1 Corinthians 1:20
That’s the breaking point.
Because what you’ve been calling “logic” might actually be distance from God.
And now you’re facing something that exposes it.
You can’t fake divine insight.
You can’t manufacture revelation.
You either receive it…
Or you don’t.
And that’s where grace enters.
Because God is not asking you to be brilliant.
He’s asking you to be dependent.
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom…” — Proverbs 9:10
Not intelligence.
Not education.
Fear of the Lord.
That means reverence.
Surrender.
Recognition that He sees what you don’t.
So when your assignment requires divine wisdom over human logic, it’s not a disadvantage.
It’s an invitation.
To stop striving.
To stop pretending you have it all together.
To stop leaning on a mind that was never meant to replace God.
And to finally say—
“I don’t know… but You do.”
That’s where clarity begins.
Not in confidence in yourself…
But in trust in Him.
And something changes when you do.
You begin to see connections you didn’t see before.
You write with a depth that doesn’t feel like it came from you.
You sense direction instead of confusion.
Not because you became smarter overnight…
But because you stepped into alignment.
“Call to Me and I will answer you and tell you great and unsearchable things you do not know.” — Jeremiah 33:3
There are things God wants to reveal to you…
But He will not compete with your pride.
So now you’re standing at a decision.
You can go back to forcing your way through this with human reasoning…
Or you can surrender and let God lead you through it.
One leads to exhaustion.
The other leads to transformation.
And this doesn’t stop with your assignment.
Because once you taste divine wisdom…
You won’t want to go back.
If something in you knows you’ve been relying too much on yourself, don’t ignore that.
Say it plainly.
“I need God’s wisdom.”
Not as a phrase.
But as surrender.
Because that’s where God starts speaking.
Follow this path if you’re ready to go deeper, where truth confronts, corrects, and transforms you beyond surface-level understanding.
